newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp confirms resignations - Journal.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp confirms resignations - Journal.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp confirmed the resignations of two more executives closely aligned with ousted chief executive Richard Scott, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
Columbia indicated more departures are likely, the newspaper said.
The two executives to leave Columbia were Herbert Wong, senior vice president for strategic development, and Jamie Hopping, president of the company's Western Group, according to the paper.
The company's general counsel, Stephen Braun, is expected to be among the next executives to resign, the Journal reported.

Columbia is at the center of a federal investigation to determine whether it defrauded the government. Columbia has been turning key documents over to the government, the paper said, which may help the U.S. calculate a fine against the company by as early as mid-October.
The fine coould be as high as $1 billion, people close to the situation told the paper.

Columbia's new chairman and chief executive, Thomas Frist -- named to head the company after Scott was ousted last month -- has made no secret of his desire to bring his own management team into the company, according to the Journal.
